thread:
alan: Heads up - onboarding demo hit a weird SDK vs REST mismatch. The Node sample app uses the streaming chat endpoint. curl works but the SDK returns the full final response (no streaming).

priya: which route/params are you using?

alan: REST curl:
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat?model=chat-3&stream=true"`
This yields SSE chunks. Node SDK call `client.chat.create({model: 'chat-3', messages, stream: true})` resolves with a single object. No events.

sdk-bot: opened issue NODE-STREAM-78: node-sdk not emitting stream events when `stream: true` set. https://git.redwood/dev/node-sdk/issues/78 :white_check_mark:

nina: hmm our Node transport used to rely on `Accept` header and response handling; the JS binding recently added a `stream` wrapper that only toggles `responseType: 'stream'` for browser fetch and forgot to hook the event parser for Node `http` responses. Looks like a regression.

diego: also noticed a subtle query-param encoding change when generating example links in the sampleapp. Arrays were serialized as `?role=assistant&role=user` in REST curl examples but the SDK sends `role[]=assistant&role[]=user` which our ingress proxy rejects with 400 in strict mode. That caused some users to see onboarding failures depending on proxy config.

priya: ouch. So two separate parity issues: streaming events not surfaced, and query array encoding differing. Any header issues?

alan: yes one more: the Node HTTP client lowercases `Authorization` causing an on-prem auth plugin to 403 sometimes. curl and other SDKs preserve header case.

sdk-bot: labels applied: sdk/node, bug, onboarding, streaming, headers. Assigned to @nina.

nina: plan: 1) rewire Node event parser for native http responses so `stream: true` returns an AsyncIterable of events (backwards-compatible wrapper to keep non-stream callers working). 2) normalize query serialization to RFC 6570-style repeated params (repeat key per value) to match REST examples, and add config `arrayFormat: 'repeat'`. 3) preserve original header casing in the low-level transport when headers are provided by callers. 4) add integration tests for streaming + proxy strict mode.

diego: short-term workaround for sampleapp: use raw fetch with explicit Accept and query string building and bypass SDK for the first whoami/onboard calls. I'll add a snippet to the README.

priya: ETA? This blocks some demos.

nina: I'll open the PR today, tests + CI might take a day. If green, we can cut a patch release tomorrow. Will post PR link and release notes here.

alan: thanks folks. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
